absent: Definitions and contracts of mount table helpers such as lookup, traversal, cloning, attachment, and unmount primitives beyond their call sites here.
User namespace capability evaluation, credential handling, and per user accounting limits.
Namespace tree identity allocation, passive versus active reference counting, and RCU lifetime rules.
Inode, namespace semaphore, mount sequence lock, and writer protection implementations and ordering guarantees beyond observed nesting.
Error pointer encoding, cleanup scope mechanics, list container behavior, and sequence retry primitives.
Superblock lifetime, path resolution, automount, dentry reference handling, and file opening semantics.
Propagation topology, peer group identity allocation, lock tree enforcement, and expiry busyness determination.
System call numbers, user flag numeric values, and binary layout guarantees for mount structures.

findings.text: Conversion from mount namespace container to generic namespace handle exposes embedded common member for namespace framework use.

Sequential mount namespace iterator advances through adjoining namespaces under RCU protection, skipping entries lacking administrative capability over owning user identity or lacking acquirable active reference, and returns first acceptable neighbor with active reference held.

Collection over a starting location plus descendant mounts builds a reference held array terminated by an empty slot, growing from caller preallocation through small then doubling then final terminator growth, validating that the starting mount remains acceptable and including only mounts beneath the starting dentry across each subtree.
Release for a collected array drops one reference per non empty entry and frees backing storage only when it differs from caller preallocation.
Subtree presence test reports true when any direct child mount point lies at or beneath a given dentry.

Private unattached duplication rejects unbindable sources and sources outside current namespace unless they form an acceptable anonymous root without disallowed namespace filesystem loops, requires administrative capability over source owner, rejects locked descendants beneath the start, clones as private and marks result internal for later kernel unmount.
Tree walk control uses two single bit indicators, one selecting beneath semantics and one selecting propagation handling, occupying the two lowest bit positions.

Mount target resolution distinguishes beneath mode, which selects the parent of the topmost overmount above the start, from normal mode, which follows any mount stacked on the start to its top and root or otherwise keeps the start itself, always returning paired mount and dentry.

Mountpoint pinning retries a sampling phase under mount read protection followed by dentry inode plus namespace acquisition and revalidation of sampled pair, refusing unmountable dentries and stale mounts and beneath requests without stacked state, and drops temporary references under namespace protection relying on stability from the still mounted start.

Unlock releases the pinned dentry inode lock, unpins the mountpoint under exclusive mount sequence protection, then releases namespace exclusivity, with outer helper acting only when pinning succeeded.
Exact copy pinning helper declares a mountpoint holder with automatic unlock on scope exit and initializes it through exact locking with copy semantics.

Detached duplicate namespace creation allocates an anonymous namespace owned by current mount owner, records origin sequence from source namespace identity while excluding concurrent attachment, duplicates the requested subtree with recursion controlled by caller, and enrolls every resulting mount with a count.

Namespace allocation accounts against per user mount namespace limit, zeroes container with accounted allocation, initializes common identity differently for anonymous versus regular cases, assigns tree generation identity, and sets single passive reference plus empty tree plus wait queue plus held user and count references, unwinding counts and storage on failure.

Detached open replaces caller path mount with root of a freshly duplicated anonymous namespace and opens it as path only, marking the resulting file to dissolve the namespace on last close and dissolving immediately if open fails.
Namespace copy control uses two single bit indicators, one requesting recursive descent and one requesting fresh single mount creation, occupying the two lowest bit positions.

New namespace construction requires lookup capability of start, forces slave plus unbindable copy treatment for foreign owners, duplicates the real root filesystem under exact copy pinning, propagates locked state from any overmount stack, either clones a single mount or duplicates a subtree with foreign non recursive callers rejected when children exist, attaches result atop the duplicated root, optionally locks whole tree for foreign owners, and enrolls all mounts with root publication.
Namespace file creation builds a new namespace from a path with given copy mode and exposes it as an open namespace file handle.
Namespace file opener consumes one caller reference while materializing a stashed path on the namespace filesystem and returns a read only open file for it, propagating lookup failure.
Open tree system entry adds returned file to descriptor table with close on exec handling and delegates to internal tree opener.

Tree opener validates flag combinations including exclusive clone versus namespace selection and recursion only with a creation mode, aligns close on exec constant with standard open flag, adjusts automount and follow behavior from caller bits, enforces administrative capability for namespace creation and general mount permission for detached cloning, resolves path with automount and follow defaults, then dispatches to namespace creation or detached duplication or plain path opening.

Peer group assignment requires exclusive namespace protection and mutability of both ends, requires both paths at mount roots on one filesystem with narrowed target beneath wider source and no locked descendants at target root, requires target private and source shared or slave, then links slave membership behind source master or joins shared group identity.
Overmount check samples mount table generation with RCU lookup and only on generation change repeats under exclusive mount sequence protection, reporting stacked presence.

Exact mount locking acquires dentry inode then namespace, refuses unmountable dentries and busy stacked targets when not copying, pins the mountpoint, then either duplicates the mount for copy mode or retains the existing mount, unwinding both locks and pin on failure.
Expiry registration appends a mount to caller expiry list under mount read protection.

Expiration reaping under namespace exclusive plus mount writer protection moves mounts from candidate list to graveyard only when still mounted and on second marking pass and not busy including propagation, then drains graveyard rechecking busyness and either returning busy entries or touching namespace generation and unmounting with propagation and synchronous semantics.

Mount option copying returns null for absent input, otherwise allocates one page and copies from user with fallback to bytewise retrieval for architectures without exact copy, reporting fault when nothing was readable and memory failure on allocation failure.
Mount string copying returns null for absent input and otherwise duplicates a bounded user string up to path maximum length.
Mount by directory name resolves target with follow semantics and reference held cleanup then delegates to path based mount with supplied device type flags and data.

Namespace duplication shares existing namespace with extra reference when new namespace flag is clear, otherwise allocates owned namespace, selects copy treatment for empty versus full and slave treatment for foreign owners, duplicates root alone or whole tree, locks result for foreign owners, publishes root, then for empty mode resets filesystem root and working directory to cloned root while for full mode walks old and new trees in parallel enrolling mounts and redirecting matching root and working directory references, skipping uncopied binding subtrees.

Subtree mount creates an anonymous namespace owned by initial user identity to host a supplied mount, looks up a named descendant with follow and automount, releases namespace reference, then exchanges mount reference for active superblock reference, write locks superblock against unmount, and returns the target dentry.
Namespace release drops active reference and only on last reference acquires exclusive namespace plus mount writer protection to record emptied namespace and unmount whole tree.

Observed mount namespace state comprises embedded common handle, owning user reference, root mount pointer, mount count, red black mount index, poll wait queue, passive reference count, anonymity indicator, origin sequence value, and per user accounting reference.

Observed mount state comprises public handle, namespace membership, parent and overmount links, mountpoint dentry, child list linkage, master plus slave plus share propagation links with group identity, expiry list linkage with one shot mark, and lock related flags.

Dropping temporary mount and dentry references while holding namespace exclusivity is safe only because the still mounted start pins the reachable chain; a missed stability check would permit use after free.

Expiry uses a one shot mark cleared by reference release, so a mount must be observed twice before reaping and must be rechecked for propagation busyness after graveyard move because an earlier unmount may have relocated busy state.
Collecting paths must terminate the array with an empty slot and hold references before returning, otherwise iteration in release would overrun and entries could disappear.
User option copying must handle partial exact copy by completing bytewise and must distinguish total fault from partial success to avoid leaking uninitialized page content.
Lock order observed is dentry inode before namespace before mount writer, with mount locked reader or sequence protection nested inside for sampling and unpinning.
Open tree progresses through flag validation, permission gating, path resolution, then exactly one terminal branch among namespace file, detached unmount on close file, or plain path file.
